lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen and read.

details: Listen and read consolidates the unit's language within a narrative context. Students read and listen to understand the plot, follow the dialogue, and comprehend the story's humorous conclusion, as well as learn new words.
Look for students actively following the text as they listen, and watch for their reactions (smiles or laughter) to the funny ending when Tim reveals what he brought.

“Let's join our friends Minh, Rosa, and Tim on their picnic! They have all brought their own picnic baskets, and I'm very curious to see what's inside each one. Let's listen and read to find out what they all brought for lunch.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Choose or write the correct answers.

details: Choose or write the correct answers checks students' comprehension of the story. The mixed-format questions require them to recall specific details about what each character brought to the picnic.
Look for the correct picture choice for question 1, the correct text choice for question 2, and the correctly written words ("fork" and "spoon") for question 3.

“That was a funny ending! Now, let's see if we were paying attention to all the details. I have some questions about what each person brought. Please choose or write the correct answers to show what you remember.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - A Read and correct a - e.

details: Read and correct develops proofreading skills and reinforces grammar. Students must carefully read the text to find and correct five specific errors related to quantifiers and plural forms.
Look for the five corrected phrases written accurately on the lines below the text.

“I was writing down the picnic story, but I think I made some grammar mistakes. I need your expert help! Can you please read my story carefully, find the five errors, and write the corrections for me?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - B Read and circle T (True) or F (False).

details: Read and circle T or F assesses reading for specific detail. Students must read each statement and decide if it is true or false based on a careful reading of the corrected story.
Look for accurately circled answers (T or F) for all four statements, showing a clear comprehension of the story's facts.
“Thank you for correcting my story! Now that it's perfect, let's do a final fact-check. Please read these statements and circle True or False to confirm all the details are correct.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - C Look and write.

details: Look and write consolidates the new vocabulary from the reading lesson. Students use the picture clues to complete the spelling of the key words, reinforcing their memory of the new items.
Look for the three key vocabulary words spelled correctly on the lines.
“For this task, let's review the new words we learned from the story. I've started writing them, but I can't remember the full spelling. Can you look at the pictures and complete them for me?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - C Imagine you and your friend are on a picnic. Write and share.

details: Write and share provides a free-production task for the lesson. Students use the prompts to write about an imagined picnic, then share their ideas with a partner to exchange information.
Look for logically completed written answers that use the target vocabulary and quantifiers correctly. Listen for confident sharing and interaction between partners using “How many/much...?.”

“We've read about Tim's funny picnic. Now, let's imagine our own! First, write down what you brought. Then, interview your friend to find out what's in their basket, because good friends always share their food at a picnic!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

The Presentation serves as a culminating, productive task for the unit. Students use a template to write a personalized version of the picnic story, then present it to the class to demonstrate their command of the language.
Look for a logically and grammatically completed story that uses the unit's language correctly, and listen for a clear, confident, and audible presentation delivered to the class.

“For our presentation, you get to be the star of the picnic story! Your mission is to use this template to write your own version, including your friend's name and the food you brought. Afterwards, you will present your story to the class.”
